read_from: The route text as served: field 1 (the route text) of each row of the route store on the main branch at commit 546df10654d7, store_version 7b3c475ce1a3 (its index.json; the served extract scratch/by-source-served-r2/conceptnet_5_7_hebrew_english_cc_by_sa_4_0.jsonl), for "ConceptNet 5.7 exact Hebrew-English lexical assertions (CC BY-SA 4.0 edge)" (M1): 10,023 routes (axis: routes), 8,269 letters keys (axis: keys). This is the store after the serving lane's retext of 6 November 2026 under row-strike-rule-v3: on every row the route text now equals the row's definition slot, the word as ConceptNet gives it (10,023 of 10,023 routes, axis: routes), and 0 routes hold a round bracket. The tag in round brackets that this corpus's own script wrote from the source's node path («he (n, wikt, en 2)» in v113) stands on no served route, so the shapes that read it and the two branches that asked about it are gone from this ledger; v113's declaration, which read the store at commit 306f3b285898, store_version 87b13b1169b4, with 11,378 routes and 18,928 mark occurrences, stands whole in mend-r2/before/. The source's own key to its signs: its changelog is on file (<home>/Documents/999 footsteps/corpus-lane/moses-ledgers-2026-09-22/moses-works-own-stamp-v1/verify-the-snapshots-and-releases/refetch/conceptnet-wiki-Changelog.md), and it settles the lowercasing of text to make a path (line 154, under ConceptNet 5.5.0), which accounts for the small letters of every route (0 routes hold a capital letter) and for the combining dot on «i̇zmir». ConceptNet's own post on the 5.7 release is also on file, at <tabernacle>/corpus-lane-builds/moses-works-own-stamp-v1/strand-3-the-publishers/fetch/conceptnet-blog-2019-conceptnet-57-released.html, which v113's relay said was not on file: a correction already sent; it settles nothing this reissue reads, since no tag stands. The marks that stand are the source's own words' marks: the apostrophe inside an English contraction or possessive, the period inside «i.e» and «e.g», and the one combining dot; every one of the 20 occurrences has a letter on both sides (axis: occurrences). All of this is evidence about the source, never a test (rule 12).

definitions.string: text compared character for character: case minded, nothing trimmed, each space the one space character U+0020. A character is one Unicode code point, whatever it is: a letter, a digit, a space or a mark. In a test or a definition a string stands between « and », which are not part of it. A list in these definitions holds its strings as JSON strings, and "one string of" a list means any one of them, whole. To begin with a string is to have that string as its first characters; no word end is needed after it.
definitions.at_top_level: the mark stands inside no bracket: the template's c.container is top.
definitions.word_around_the_mark: the longest run of letters (a letter is a character whose Unicode general category begins with L, in JavaScript \p{L}, small or capital, any script; a digit, a mark, a space or a combining mark is not a letter) that ends directly before the mark (the run may be empty), then the mark itself, then the longest run of letters that begins directly after the mark (the run may be empty). A run stops at the first character that is not a letter, and at the start or the end of the route text.

shapes.means: stands inside the English abbreviation «i.e» or «e.g», which is itself the whole text of its route and which is written with no period after its last letter.
shapes.test: A period at_top_level whose word_around_the_mark is one string of abbreviations_in_the_word.

shapes.means: joins the two parts of an English contraction in the words the source gives: «i'm», «you're», «don't», «let's» or «that's».
shapes.test: An apostrophe at_top_level whose word_around_the_mark is one string of contraction_words.

shapes.means: marks the English possessive in the words the source gives: «adam's apple», «men's», «one's» or «year's».
shapes.test: An apostrophe at_top_level whose word_around_the_mark is one string of possessive_words.

shapes.means: stands on a small «i», and the one route that holds such a dot is the name «i̇zmir»: the source's changelog says it lowercases text to make its path, and lowercasing a capital dotted I gives a small i with this dot, while no route of this dictionary holds a capital letter; that this name was written with that capital is a reading, for the capital stands on no row of this dictionary's extract, though the source's own assertions file writes the name with it.
shapes.test: A combining dot above at_top_level with the string «i» directly before it (any small i).

homonyms.reason: The source has no entries: it holds edges between a Hebrew node and an English node, and a route rests on one such edge or, since the retext folded the tagged rows into the bare word, on every edge of this licence whose English word is that text under that key. A number that stood in a tag («en 1», «en 2») stood in the English node's path and told nothing about the Hebrew word; it prints nowhere now. Key אדר holds «adar», «maple» and «pleural cavity», and the route text cannot say whether they are senses of one word or two words. Of the keys this count holds, 1,356 of 8,269 hold more than one route text (axis: keys), each text a different English word now that no key holds one word under two tags.
